parsedVerdict.reasoning: The orchestration in execute() is a proper application-layer job: it checks that the product exists, then calls the repository to delete it. The @CommandHandler decorator is ordinary NestJS CQRS wiring for a use case, so I accept it here. The problem is the failure path. When the product is missing, the handler throws NotFoundException from @nestjs/common. That is an HTTP exception that maps to a 404 response, so the use case is deciding the transport-level result itself. That decision belongs to the presentation/infrastructure layer, for example a controller or an exception filter that turns an application error into an HTTP status. The use case should instead throw an application or domain error such as ProductNotFoundError. The import of the infrastructure ProductRepository is an import-direction issue, so it is out of scope and not judged. My confidence is moderate because many NestJS codebases accept this pattern.
